newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Dominion sees progress on nickel find.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Dominion sees progress on nickel find.

text.p: Dominion Mining Ltd expects to make "tangible" headway toward development of its Yakabindie nickel/cobalt project in Western Australia in the next two months, managing dirctor Ken Dredge said on Tuesday.
"In two months time, we expect to see something tangible happening that will put us well on the way to announcing a partner for Yakabindie," Dredge told Reuters.

He said revised mining reserves and formulation of a new mine plan had made the A$500 milion project more attractive since miner North Ltd decided in December last year not to take up an option for an 80 percent stake.

Yakabindie could begin production by mid-1997, up to 12 months earlier than originally scheduled, and produce up to 30,000 tonnes per year of nickel metal by the end of calendar 1998, Dominion has said.
The project has the potential to produce overall between 600,000 and 700,000 tonnes of nickel, Dredge said.
Production costs of around US$1.61 a pound after cobalt credits were achievable at the mine, he said.
The figure takes into account credits from an anticipated average cobalt price of US$12.00 a pound, he added.
Dredge said his company was targeting a "select shortlist" of potential partners, but acknowledged these groups were also looking at other Australian nickel projects.

Testing of orebody samples had indicated an immediate increase in concentrator recovery to around 67 percent from the design sign-off of 63.7 percent is possible, Dredge said, adding a recovery in excess of 70 percent may be achievable.
A rise in recoveries would lower production costs of the project, he said.

Dominion earlier announced a 1995/1996 net profit of A$39.59 million after taking into acount abnormal profit of A$38.2 million. In the pervious year, the company recorded a loss of A$43.80 million. Dominion shares closed unchanged at A$0.70.
